feed.title: Jejak Kata: Stories
feed.subtitle: Each story sets out from a question people fight about, turns on something the counting found, and stops at the edge: what the data cannot say. Every number is a count of pages, and every one can be checked.

entry.title: Did the price rise, or was it “adjusted”?
entry.summary: “Penyesuaian harga” (price adjustment) is used almost only for prices the state sets: fuel, electricity, tolls, health insurance. Of 200 we read, 139 mean a rise, and 120 are spoken by the government or a state company.

entry.title: Who gets called “oknum”?
entry.summary: On pages about wrongdoing, the word “oknum” (a rogue individual) sits beside teachers, civil servants, soldiers and village heads more often than beside legislators or judges: two to five times in Kompas and Detik. Of 200 “oknum” we read, 150 are not named.

entry.title: Arrested, or “secured”?
entry.summary: On the police's own news site, a third of the pages about a suspect use the word “diamankan” (secured). In Tribunnews a quarter. In Kompas it rose from 5% (2011) to 15% (2024). In Tempo: 2–8%.

entry.title: No viral, no police?
entry.summary: In 2010–2014 the word “viral” is absent from news about the police. Now it is on 6–12% of those pages, two to three times the rate of all news. Village heads and school heads follow: 2–10%. On pages about the KPK, parliament, ministers and governors: below average.

entry.title: What the news stopped talking about at each change of term
entry.summary: After SBY: fuel prices, labour, clashes, and the word “didesak” (was urged). After Jokowi's first term: haze, radicalism, sting operations. The list is made by a rule, and holds only words that shrank in three outlets at once.

entry.title: A year after leaving, a fifth is left
entry.summary: A year out of office, SBY is down to 19% of his last year in Kompas, 6% in Tempo, 16% in Tribunnews. Of the 25 people who left seven top offices in 2012–2023, 23 have enough pages to count; their median is 16–25%. Those not forgotten: the ones who took another post, ran for office, or stood trial.

entry.title: Which parties get written with the word “korupsi”
entry.summary: While Demokrat governed, “korupsi” was on 17–25% of the pages naming it. While PDI Perjuangan governed: 11% at most. In 2020–2024 all ten parties that have sat in parliament since 2009 are at 2–10%.

entry.title: The KPK shrank from the news. The word “suspect” did not
entry.summary: From 2012 to 2023 the word “kpk” shrank by more than half in three outlets. But in 2024 Tempo turned back, the verbs beside the KPK never softened, and there is as much news about suspects as ever.

entry.title: From candidate to defence minister, in one year
entry.summary: Two defeats, then a seat in the cabinet. Within one year the word beside Prabowo's name went from “capres” to “menteri pertahanan”. The word “oposisi” is rare beside his name, but it is rare beside everyone's.

entry.title: The state picks a word. Newsrooms do not always follow
entry.summary: A presidential decree replaced “Cina” with “Tiongkok”: Kompas went along in 2014–2015 and then turned back, Tempo never did. But the police's term for the armed groups in Papua, “KKB”, led in all three until 2023.

entry.title: The lifespan of a slogan
entry.summary: BLSM, revolusi mental, nawacita, tol laut, tax amnesty, PSBB, new normal, PPKM. How long do a government's words last in the news before they vanish? A lighter note.
